predecessors.name: Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic
predecessors.text: the former Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast (NKAO), the Shahumyan Region and the Getashen subdistrict, as proclaimed

successors.name: Republic of Azerbaijan
successors.text: Nagorno-Karabakh, retaken in the offensive of 19-20 September 2023

ledger.x: September 1991: the Nagorno-Karabakh Republic is proclaimed.
26 February 1992: Armenian forces storm Khojaly and the war for Karabakh becomes a ground campaign.
12 May 1994: the ceasefire leaves Karabakh in the republic's hands.
12 May 1994: the ceasefire ends the first war.
27 September 2020: Azerbaijan opens the second war.
8 November 2020: Shusha falls and southern Karabakh is lost.
10 November 2020: the ceasefire ends the second war.
19-20 September 2023: Azerbaijan takes the rest of Karabakh.
28 September 2023: Artsakh decrees its own end.

wars.name: First Nagorno-Karabakh War
wars.outcome: Armenian forces took the enclave (Khojaly 26 February 1992, Shusha 8-9 May 1992, Lachin 18-19 May 1992) and, in 1993, Kalbajar (2-3 April) and districts toward Agdam, Fuzuli and Jabrayil; the ceasefire of 12 May 1994 left them 'in full control of the enclave'…

wars.name: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
wars.outcome: 27 September-10 November 2020: Azerbaijan retook Jabrayil, Fuzuli and Shusha (8 November) and 72 percent of the disputed territory; a Russian-brokered ceasefire left the republic its rump around Stepanakert.

wars.name: Azerbaijani offensive of September 2023
wars.outcome: Azerbaijan attacked on 19 September 2023, the government agreed to disarm on the 20th and decreed its institutions dissolved on 28 September, effective 1 January 2024.

certainty.note: The NKAO's former oblast boundary and the 1994 and 2020 front lines are firm lines in the sources, but Natural Earth rayons only approximate them; Shahumyan and the corridor are not drawn.
